text: In wild-type (Slc9a6+) primary mouse cortical neurons, treatment with ApoE4-conditioned medium reduced Reelin-stimulated surface expression of Apoer2 and of AMPA/NMDA receptor subunits markedly more than ApoE3-conditioned medium, indicating a stronger ApoE4-induced block of endosomal recycling (the step the authors propose drives progressive endosomal acidification); the deficit was abolished in NHE6-deficient neurons (reported: ~30% of control surface level with ApoE4 vs ~80% with ApoE3 in Slc9a6+ neurons (Apoer2)).
description: Primary cortical neurons (E18) from wild-type and germline Slc9a6- (NHE6 KO) mouse littermates, DIV10-14; pre-treated 30 min with ApoE3- or ApoE4-conditioned HEK293 medium (5 µg/ml) then 30 min Reelin (2 µg/ml); cell-surface biotinylation and immunoblot for Apoer2, GluN2B, GluA1, GluA2/3 normalized to total. Caveat: mouse neurons, not human astrocytes; readout is receptor surface level, not endosomal pH.

provenance.excerpt: (C-F) ApoE-conditioned media treatment reduces the surface expression of Apoer2 and glutamate receptors in presence of Reelin in primary neurons. Receptor surface levels show a stronger reduction with ApoE4 than ApoE3. NHE6 depletion counteracts the ApoE4-induced reduction of receptor surface expression.

meccogFinding.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater block of Reelin-stimulated Apoer2/glutamate receptor recycling to the neuronal surface) -> [inferred delayed endosomal maturation/acidification]

measured.variable: Cell-surface levels (surface biotinylation / total) of Apoer2, GluN2B, GluA1 and GluA2/3 after Reelin stimulation — a readout of endosomal recycling, used by the authors to infer the ApoE4-induced early-endosomal trafficking/acidification defect
